code.nameAr: The Battle for Your Cyber Security
code.topicAr: Defend your homeland, your identity and your cyber security
code.bossNameAr: The Storm of the Cyber War

M1.C1.feedbackAr: News with no source isn't news yet. Before you believe it, look for it on the official account of the body concerned.
M1.C1.hintAr: Who said this? Did the official body itself say it?

M1.C2.feedbackAr: A message that begs to be shared needs a pause. Don't send what you haven't checked: a rumour stops when it stops with you.
M1.C2.hintAr: Why does it insist you share it? Have you checked it yourself?

M1.C3.feedbackAr: Pictures and voices can be faked with AI today. If a well-known person seems to say something odd, check their official account and don't share the clip.
M1.C3.hintAr: Is seeing a clip enough to believe it? Where is the original?

M2.C1.feedbackAr: When a clip doesn't fit our values and upbringing: skip it, tap “Not interested” or “Report”, and tell your parents. The app shows more of what you watch more.
M2.C1.hintAr: The app learns from what you watch. What should it show you tomorrow?

M2.C2.feedbackAr: Not everything that spreads is worth copying. Don't join or film a challenge that hurts or insults. Warn your friends and tell an adult.
M2.C2.hintAr: If nobody were filming, would you still do it?

M2.C3.feedbackAr: Whoever mocks our customs and symbols wants your anger and replies to spread. Don't argue or insult: report, block, and be calmly proud of who you are.
M2.C3.hintAr: What does the account want from you? What happens to its post when you reply?

M3.C1.labelAr: A photo that shows where you are
M3.C1.feedbackAr: A photo can tell strangers where you live, study and are right now. Post after you leave, only to people you know, and hide the location and its clues.
M3.C1.hintAr: What can a stranger learn from this photo alone?

M3.C2.feedbackAr: A fun quiz that asks for your full name, birthday, school and family's numbers is collecting your data. Don't trade your personal details for a game.
M3.C2.hintAr: Why would a fun quiz need your full name and your dad's number?

M3.C3.feedbackAr: Make your account private and accept only people you know in real life. A follower count is worth nothing next to your privacy and your family's.
M3.C3.hintAr: Do you open your door to everyone who knocks?

M4.C1.labelAr: A stranger's request in a game
M4.C1.feedbackAr: Someone in a game who asks for a private chat, a photo or a secret is not acting like a friend. Say no, stop the chat, and tell your parents.
M4.C1.hintAr: A real friend never asks you to hide things from your family. So who does?

M4.C2.feedbackAr: Mocking a classmate in a group is bullying. Don't join in or answer with insults: save the proof, support your classmate, and tell an adult you trust.
M4.C2.hintAr: If you were them, what would you want your friends to do?

M4.C3.labelAr: An account posing as someone known
M4.C3.feedbackAr: Before you believe an account named after a known person or body, find the verified official account, and send no money or details.
M4.C3.hintAr: Anyone can copy a name and photo. What proves an account is real?

M5.C1.feedbackAr: Many accounts are not proof: fakes are made by the hundred to look like public opinion. Check who they are and when they were made, and don't be carried along.
M5.C1.hintAr: Do numbers prove the truth? Who are these accounts repeating one sentence?

M5.C2.labelAr: An invite to an unknown group
M5.C2.feedbackAr: A closed group that stirs anger or promises secrets is no place for you. Don't join, leave if you were added, and tell your parents.
M5.C2.hintAr: Why would a group you don't know want to stay closed and secret?

M5.C3.labelAr: Your news source in a crisis
M5.C3.feedbackAr: Rumours multiply in a crisis. Take news from official sources: the news agency, the weather office, civil defence and your school, not a forwarded voice note.
M5.C3.hintAr: Who is in charge of announcing this? Did you hear it from them?
